newsitem.title: USA: CBOT March contracts expire quietly at 1201 CST.
newsitem.headline: CBOT March contracts expire quietly at 1201 CST.

text.p: CBOT March grain and soy complex contracts expired without fanfare Wednesday at 1201 CST/1800 GMT, traders said.

Floor sources said soymeal was the feature during expiration. The March soymeal contract settled $2.90 per ton higher at $275.70 a ton. Produce Grain, Harris Bank, Prudential Securities and Smith Barney were late buyer of March soymeal but those transactions were completed before the expiration session. ADM Investor Services spread 150 lots of May/March and Smith Barney did 100 lots of March/May, traders said.
March soyoil settled 0.09 cent per lb lower at 24.26 cents per lb.
March corn settled 3-1/2 cents per bushel lower at $3.02-1/2. Refco Inc was a late purchaser of 300,000 bushels, traders said.
The March soybean contract ended 5-3/4 cents lower at $8.21-3/4 with mainly light local trading, they said.
The oat contract dropped 7-1/2 cents into expiration and settled at $1.88 per bushel while March rice tumbled 23 cents per cwt and settled at $11.50 per cwt.
Rice traders said LFG Futures sold five lots of March with E.D. and F. Man International and Dean Witter also sellers of the March into the expiration.
March wheat expired up one cent at $3.78 per bushel with E.D. and F. Man International a late spreader of 200,000 bushels of March/May.
"I don't see anything too exciting, certainly nothing compared to a year ago," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
The expirations of the March contracts Wednesday were likened to a "walk in the park" compared with the surge in the March 1996 contract to a record $7.50 per bushel on March 20, 1996.
But the March corn contract early this week was looking suspiciously vulnerable to volatile dealings during Wednesday's expiration.
Open interest in that month stood at roughly 43 million bushels early Monday but the market drew out about 36 million bushels of that in two trading sessions amid relatively rational price movements.
The preliminary open interest total for March corn early Wednesday stood at 7.6 million bushels, a little on the high side for expiration day but a level viewed by traders as "tolerable."

Open interest levels in March wheat and in the March soy complex were drawn down to manageable levels as early as Monday's trading session and only the usual "mild" fireworks were expected by traders during the expiration of the March in those commodities.

Early Wednesday, the CBOT reported the preliminary open interest in March soybeans at 2.37 million bushels, March soymeal at 444 lots and soyoil at 916 lots. Open interest in March wheat stood at 865,000 bushels and in March oats it stood at 430,000 bushels.
